title.zh: 卷五十五 列傳第三十六 孝義
title.raw: 卷五十五 列傳第三十六 孝義 Volume 55 Biographies 36: Filial Piety

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷第五十五‧列傳第三十六 孝義

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 55, Biographies 36: Filial Piety and Righteous Conduct
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 55, Biography 36: Filial Piety and Righteous Conduct

sentences.zh: 崔懷慎 公孫僧遠 吳欣之 韓係伯 孫淡 華寶 韓靈敏 封延伯 吳達之 王文殊 朱謙之 蕭叡明 樂頤 江泌 杜栖 陸絳

translations.literal: Cui Huaishen, Gongsun Sengyuan, Wu Xinzhi, Han Xibo, Sun Dan, Hua Bao, Han Lingmin, Feng Yanbo, Wu Dazhi, Wang Wenshu, Zhu Qianzhi, Xiao Ruiming, Le Yi, Jiang Bi, Du Qi, and Lu Jiang
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huaishen, Gongsun Sengyuan, Wu Xinzhi, Han Xibo, Sun Dan, Hua Bao, Han Lingmin, Feng Yanbo, Wu Dazhi, Wang Wenshu, Zhu Qianzhi, Xiao Ruiming, Le Yi, Jiang Bi, Du Qi, and Lu Jiang

sentences.zh: 子曰：「父子之道，天性也，君臣之義也。」

translations.literal: The Master said: "The way between father and son is innate nature; it is also the principle governing ruler and minister."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "The bond between father and son is rooted in nature itself, yet it also embodies the duty owed between ruler and subject."

sentences.zh: 人之含孝稟義，天生所同，淳薄因心，非俟學至。

translations.literal: Human beings embody filial piety and are endowed with righteousness—what all share from birth; whether one is pure or coarse depends on the heart, not on waiting for learning to arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Filial devotion and moral duty are inborn in every person alike; whether they flourish or wither depends on the heart, not on formal instruction."

sentences.zh: 遲遇為用，不謝始庶之法，驕慢之性，多慚水菽之享。

translations.literal: When circumstances delay its exercise, one does not decline the method of the first concubine's son; those of a proud and arrogant nature are often ashamed to offer only water and coarse beans in feasting.
translations.idiomatic: When fortune delays the chance to act, one need not reject the humblest ways of honoring parents; the proud and arrogant, by contrast, are often ashamed to serve no more than plain water and simple fare.

sentences.zh: 夫色養盡力，行義致身，甘心壟畝，不求聞達，斯即孟氏三樂之辭，仲由負米之歎也。

translations.literal: To nourish parents with cheerful countenance and exert all one's strength, to practice righteousness even at the cost of one's person, to be content in the fields and not seek fame or advancement—this is what Mencius called the three joys, and what Zhong You sighed over when carrying rice on his back.
translations.idiomatic: To serve one's parents with a joyful face and every ounce of strength, to live by righteousness even at risk to oneself, and to be content tilling the soil without seeking renown—this is the joy Mencius praised and the devotion Zhong You expressed when he carried rice for his parents.

sentences.zh: 通乎神明，理緣感召。

translations.literal: When it penetrates to the spirits, principle operates through sympathetic response.
translations.idiomatic: When filial feeling reaches the realm of spirits, principle itself moves through sympathetic response.

sentences.zh: 情澆世薄，方表孝慈。

translations.literal: When sentiment runs thin and the age grows shallow, only then do filial piety and kindness stand forth in relief.
translations.idiomatic: Only when human feeling runs thin and the age grows coarse does true filial kindness show itself plainly.

sentences.zh: 故非內德者所以寄心，懷仁者所以標物矣。

translations.literal: Therefore those without inner virtue have nowhere to lodge the heart, while those who cherish benevolence thereby mark out what matters.
translations.idiomatic: Those without inner virtue have nowhere to set their hearts, while those who cherish benevolence thereby show what truly counts in the world.

sentences.zh: 埋名韞節，鮮或昭著，紀夫事行，以列于篇。

translations.literal: They bury their names and restrain their conduct, and few become widely known; I record their deeds and actions here to set them forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Most such people hide their names and restrain their conduct, and few ever become widely known; I therefore record their deeds here in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 崔懷慎，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Huaishen was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huaishen was from Dongwucheng in Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 父邪利，魯郡太守，宋元嘉中，沒虜。

translations.literal: His father Xieli was Administrator of Lu commandery; during the Yuanjia era of the Song, he was captured by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xieli had been Administrator of Lu commandery; during Emperor Wen's Yuanjia reign he was captured by the northern invaders.

sentences.zh: 懷慎與妻房氏篤愛，聞父陷沒，即日遣妻，布衣蔬食，如居喪禮。

translations.literal: Huaishen and his wife, née Fang, were deeply devoted to each other; when he heard that his father had fallen into captivity, that very day he sent his wife away, wore coarse cloth and ate plain vegetables, and observed the rites as though in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishen and his wife Lady Fang loved each other deeply. When he learned his father had been taken captive, he dismissed his wife that same day, dressed in hemp and ate only plain food, and lived as though in mourning.

sentences.zh: 邪利後仕虜中書，戒懷慎不許如此，懷慎得書更號泣。

translations.literal: Xieli later served the barbarians as Director of the Secretariat and admonished Huaishen not to behave in this way; when Huaishen received the letter, he wept and wailed all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Xieli later served the northerners as Director of the Secretariat and urged Huaishen not to go on like this; when Huaishen read the letter, he wept all the harder.

sentences.zh: 懷慎從叔模為滎陽太守，亦同沈虜，模子雖居處改節，而不廢婚宦。

translations.literal: Huaishen's paternal uncle Mo was Administrator of Xingyang and likewise sank into captivity among the barbarians; Mo's son, though he altered his conduct in daily life, did not abandon marriage or office.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishen's uncle Mo, Administrator of Xingyang, was also taken by the northerners. Mo's son changed his way of life under captivity but still married and took office.

sentences.zh: 大明中，懷慎宗人冀州刺史元孫北使，虜問之曰：「崔邪利、模竝力屈歸命，二家子姪，出處不同，義將安在？」

translations.literal: During the Daming era, Huaishen's clansman Yuansun, Governor of Jizhou, went north on a mission; the barbarians asked him: "Cui Xieli and Mo both, their strength exhausted, submitted and pledged allegiance—yet the sons and nephews of the two families differ in where they stand and what they do. Where does righteousness lie?"
translations.idiomatic: During the Daming era Huaishen's kinsman Yuansun, governor of Jizhou, went north on a mission. The northerners asked him: "Cui Xieli and Mo both submitted when their strength gave out, yet their sons and nephews behave differently. Where does righteousness lie?"

sentences.zh: 元孫曰：「王尊驅驥，王陽回車，欲令忠孝竝弘，臣子兩節。」

translations.literal: Yuansun replied: "Wang Zun drove his thoroughbred on, while Wang Yang turned his carriage back—each wished to make loyalty and filial piety flourish together, fulfilling both the minister's and the son's obligations."
translations.idiomatic: Yuansun replied: "Wang Zun drove his horse forward while Wang Yang turned his carriage back—each sought to honor both loyalty and filial duty, fulfilling the obligations of subject and son alike."

sentences.zh: 泰始初，淮北陷沒，界上流奔者，多有去就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taishi era, the north bank of the Huai fell; among those who fled across the border upstream, many wavered between staying and leaving.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taishi era the north Huai region fell, and many refugees who fled south across the border wavered between staying and returning.

sentences.zh: 懷慎因此入北。

translations.literal: Because of this, Huaishen went north.
translations.idiomatic: On this account Huaishen went north himself.

sentences.zh: 至桑乾，邪利時已卒，懷慎絕而後蘇。

translations.literal: When he reached Sanggan, Xieli had already died; Huaishen lost consciousness and only afterward revived.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Sanggan he found Xieli had already died; Huaishen fainted and only later came to.

sentences.zh: 載喪還青州，徒跣冰雪，土氣寒酷，而手足不傷，時人以為孝感。

translations.literal: He carried the coffin back to Qingzhou, walking barefoot through ice and snow; though the climate was bitterly cold, his hands and feet were uninjured, and people of the time took this as a response to filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: He bore the coffin back to Qingzhou, walking barefoot through ice and snow. Though the cold was fierce, his hands and feet were unharmed, and people regarded it as a sign of filial devotion moving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 喪畢，以弟在南，建元初，又逃歸，而弟亦已亡。

translations.literal: When the mourning was finished, because his younger brother was in the south, at the beginning of the Jianyuan era he fled back south again, but his brother had already died.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period, knowing his younger brother was in the south, he fled back at the start of the Jianyuan era—only to find his brother had already died.

sentences.zh: 懷慎孤貧獨立，宗黨哀之，日斂給其升米。

translations.literal: Huaishen was left alone, poor and isolated; his clan pitied him and each day collected and gave him measures of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishen was left alone in poverty; his kinsmen pitied him and each day pooled their grain to support him.

sentences.zh: 永明中卒。

translations.literal: He died during the Yongming era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Yongming era.

sentences.zh: 公孫僧遠，會稽剡人也。

translations.literal: Gongsun Sengyuan was a native of Shan in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Sengyuan was from Shan county in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 治父喪至孝，事母及伯父甚謹，年饑穀貴，僧遠省餐減食，以供母、伯。

translations.literal: In observing mourning for his father he was supremely filial; in serving his mother and his father's elder brother he was most careful. In years of famine when grain was dear, Sengyuan reduced his own meals to supply his mother and uncle.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply filial in mourning his father and scrupulous in caring for his mother and uncle. In famine years, when grain was costly, he ate less himself so that they might have enough.

sentences.zh: 弟亡，無以葬，身販貼與隣里，供斂送之費。

translations.literal: When his younger brother died and there was no means to bury him, he sold himself on bond to his neighbors to provide the expenses of encoffining and burial.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother died and he had no money for the funeral, he indentured himself to neighbors to pay for the burial.

sentences.zh: 躬負土，手種松柏。

translations.literal: He personally carried earth on his back and planted pine and cypress with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: He carried the earth for the grave himself and planted pine and cypress trees with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 兄姊未婚嫁，乃自賣為之成禮。

translations.literal: His elder brother and sister were still unmarried, so he sold himself again to provide for their weddings.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother and sister were still unmarried, so he sold himself once more to provide for their weddings.

sentences.zh: 名聞郡縣。

translations.literal: His fame spread through the commandery and county.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation spread throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，遣兼散騎常侍虞炎等十二部使行天下，建元三年，表列僧遠等二十三人，詔竝表門閭，蠲租稅。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, he dispatched twelve groups of envoys led by Acting Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Yu Yan and others to travel throughout the realm; in the third year of Jianyuan, memorials listed Sengyuan and twenty-two others, and an edict ordered that their household gates all be honored with commemorative placards and that their rents and taxes be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao took the throne he sent twelve missions, led by Yu Yan, Acting Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, to tour the empire. In the third year of Jianyuan, memorials named Sengyuan and twenty-two others; an edict ordered commemorative placards erected at their gates and their rents and taxes remitted.

sentences.zh: 吳欣之，晉陵利城人也。

translations.literal: Wu Xinzhi was a native of Licheng in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xinzhi was from Licheng in Jinling commandery.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉末，弟尉之為武進縣戍，隨王誕起義，太初遣軍主華欽討之，吏民皆散，尉之獨留，見執將死。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanjia era of Song, his younger brother Weizhi was garrisoned at Wujin county; when Prince Dan of Sui raised a rebellion, during the Taichu era troops were sent under Commander Hua Qin to suppress it; officials and commoners all fled, but Weizhi alone remained, was seized, and was about to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuanjia era his brother Weizhi was stationed at Wujin. When Prince Dan of Sui rebelled, the court sent Commander Hua Qin against him. Officials and commoners fled, but Weizhi alone stayed behind, was captured, and was about to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 欣之詣欽乞代弟命，辭淚哀切，兄弟皆見原。

translations.literal: Xinzhi went to Qin and begged to die in his brother's place; his words and tears were bitterly moving, and both brothers were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhi went to Qin and begged to die in his brother's place, weeping with such anguish that both brothers were spared.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，有詔蠲表。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan, an edict granted him remission and public commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan an edict honored him with remission of taxes and a commemorative placard.

sentences.zh: 永明初，廣陵民章起之二息犯罪爭死，太守劉悛表以聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming, a man of Guangling named Zhang Qi had two sons who, having committed a crime, each vied to die in the other's place; the Administrator Liu Jun memorialized this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongming, a Guangling man named Zhang Qi had two sons who, after committing a crime, each insisted on dying in the other's stead; Administrator Liu Jun reported this to the court.

sentences.zh: 韓係伯，襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Han Xibo was a native of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xibo was from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 事父母謹孝。

translations.literal: In serving his parents he was careful and filial.
translations.idiomatic: He served his parents with scrupulous filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 襄陽土俗，隣居種桑樹於界上為誌，係伯以桑枝蔭妨他地，遷堺上開數尺，隣畔隨復侵之，係伯輙更改種。

translations.literal: By custom in Xiangyang, neighbors planted mulberry trees on the boundary as markers; Xibo's mulberry branches shaded the neighboring plot, so he moved his trees several feet inside the boundary, but the neighbor at once encroached again, and Xibo each time shifted and replanted.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiangyang custom neighbors planted mulberries on the boundary as markers. When Xibo's trees shaded the next plot, he moved them several feet inward; the neighbor encroached again at once, and each time Xibo simply moved and replanted his trees.

sentences.zh: 久之，隣人慚愧，還所侵地，躬往謝之。

translations.literal: After a long while the neighbor felt ashamed, returned the land he had seized, and came in person to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: In time the neighbor was ashamed, returned the land he had taken, and came in person to apologize.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，蠲租稅，表門閭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan, his rents and taxes were remitted and a commemorative placard was erected at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan his taxes were remitted and a commemorative placard was set up at his gate.

sentences.zh: 以壽終。

translations.literal: He died at the end of his natural span.
translations.idiomatic: He died at a ripe old age.

sentences.zh: 孫淡，太原人也。

translations.literal: Sun Dan was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Dan was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 居長沙，事母孝，母疾，不眠食，以差為期。

translations.literal: He lived in Changsha and was filial toward his mother; when she fell ill, he neither slept nor ate, taking her recovery as his only measure.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Changsha and was devoted to his mother. When she fell ill he neither slept nor ate, counting each day only by whether she improved.

sentences.zh: 母哀之，後有疾，不使知也。

translations.literal: His mother pitied him; afterward, whenever she fell ill, she did not let him know.
translations.idiomatic: His mother pitied him; after that, whenever she fell ill she kept it from him.

sentences.zh: 豫章王領湘州，辟驃騎行參軍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang, holding Xiangzhou, summoned him as Aide on the March of the Rapid Tiger General.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yuzhang governed Xiangzhou he summoned Dan as an aide in the Rapid Tiger General's staff.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，蠲租稅，表門閭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan, his rents and taxes were remitted and a commemorative placard was erected at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan his taxes were remitted and a commemorative placard was set up at his gate.

sentences.zh: 卒于家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 華寶，晉陵無錫人也。

translations.literal: Hua Bao was a native of Wuxi in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Bao was from Wuxi in Jinling commandery.

sentences.zh: 父豪，義熙末，戍長安，寶年八歲。

translations.literal: His father Hao, at the end of the Yixi era, was garrisoned at Chang'an; Bao was eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hao was posted to Chang'an at the end of the Yixi era, when Bao was eight.

sentences.zh: 臨別，謂寶曰：「須我還，當為汝上頭。」

translations.literal: On parting he said to Bao: "When I return, I shall arrange your capping ceremony for you."
translations.idiomatic: As he left he told Bao: "When I come back, I will cap you myself."

sentences.zh: 長安陷虜，豪歿。

translations.literal: Chang'an fell to the barbarians and Hao died.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an fell to the invaders and Hao died.

sentences.zh: 寶年至七十，不婚冠，或問之者，輙號慟彌日，不忍答也。

translations.literal: When Bao reached seventy he had neither married nor undergone the capping ceremony; if anyone asked him about it, he would wail and lament for whole days and could not bear to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Bao lived to seventy without marrying or being capped; if anyone asked why, he would wail for days on end and could not bring himself to reply.

sentences.zh: 同郡薛天生，母遭艱菜食，天生亦菜食，母未免喪而死，天生終身不食魚肉。

translations.literal: In the same commandery, Xue Tiansheng's mother, during her mourning period, ate only vegetables; Tiansheng also ate only vegetables. Before she had completed her mourning she died, and Tiansheng never ate fish or meat for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the same commandery, Xue Tiansheng's mother ate only vegetables while in mourning, and he did the same. She died before the mourning period ended, and he never ate fish or meat again as long as he lived.

sentences.zh: 與弟有恩義。

translations.literal: With his younger brother he shared bonds of kindness and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply devoted to his younger brother.

sentences.zh: 又同郡劉懷胤與弟懷則，年十歲，遭父喪，不衣絮帛，不食鹽菜。

translations.literal: Also in the same commandery, Liu Huaiyin and his younger brother Huaize, at ten years of age when their father died, wore neither padded silk nor ate salted vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: In the same commandery, Liu Huaiyin and his brother Huaize were only ten when their father died; they wore no silk padding and ate neither salt nor seasoned vegetables.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，竝表門閭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan, commemorative placards were erected at their gates alike.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan commemorative placards were set up at their gates.

sentences.zh: 韓靈敏，會稽剡人也。

translations.literal: Han Lingmin was a native of Shan in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingmin was from Shan in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 早孤，與兄靈珍竝有孝性，尋母又亡，家貧無以營凶，兄弟共種衆半畝，朝採衆子，暮已復生，以此遂辦葬事。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he and his elder brother Lingzhen were both filial by nature; soon their mother also died, and the family was too poor to arrange the funeral. The brothers together planted half an acre of amaranth; they gathered the seeds in the morning, and by evening the plants had grown again—by this means they were able to complete the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he and his elder brother Lingzhen were both deeply filial. When their mother died the family was too poor for a funeral. Together they planted half an acre of amaranth, gathered the seeds each morning, and found the plants grown again by evening—enough to pay for the burial.

sentences.zh: 靈珍亡，無子，妻卓氏守節不嫁，慮家人奪其志，未嘗告歸，靈敏事之如母。

translations.literal: When Lingzhen died without sons, his wife, née Zhuo, kept her chastity and would not remarry; fearing the family might force her to change her resolve, she never announced visits home, and Lingmin served her as though she were his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingzhen died childless, his widow Lady Zhuo refused to remarry. Fearing the family would break her resolve, she never went home to visit; Lingmin served her as he would a mother.

sentences.zh: 晉陵吳康之妻趙氏，父亡弟幼，值歲饑，母老病篤，趙詣鄉里自賣，言辭哀苦，鄉里憐之，人人分升米相救，遂得免。

translations.literal: Zhao, wife of Wu Kangzhi of Jinling—her father was dead and her younger brother still a child; in a year of famine her mother was old and gravely ill. Zhao went among the villagers offering to sell herself; her words were bitterly moving, the villagers pitied her, and each person gave a portion of grain until she was saved.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhao, wife of Wu Kangzhi of Jinling, had lost her father and had a young brother to support. In a famine year her aged mother fell gravely ill. Zhao offered herself for sale in the village with such anguish that neighbors each gave grain until the family was saved.

sentences.zh: 及嫁康之，少時夫亡，家欲更嫁，誓死不貳。

translations.literal: When she married Kangzhi, before long her husband died; the family wished to marry her again, but she vowed she would die rather than take another husband.
translations.idiomatic: After she married Kangzhi her husband soon died. The family wanted her to remarry, but she swore she would die before taking another husband.

sentences.zh: 義興蔣儁之妻黃氏，夫亡不重嫁，逼之，欲赴水自殺，乃止。

translations.literal: Lady Huang, wife of Jiang Junzhi of Yixing—when her husband died she would not remarry; when pressed, she tried to throw herself into the water to die, and only then did they desist.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huang of Yixing, wife of Jiang Junzhi, refused to remarry after her husband's death. When the family pressed her, she tried to drown herself, and only then did they relent.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，詔蠲租賦，表門閭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan, an edict remitted their rents and levies and erected commemorative placards at their gates.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan an edict remitted their taxes and honored their gates with commemorative placards.

sentences.zh: 又廣陵徐靈禮妻遭火救兒，與兒俱焚死。

translations.literal: Also, the wife of Xu Lingli of Guangling, when fire broke out, rushed to save her child and perished in the flames together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Also in Guangling, the wife of Xu Lingli ran into a fire to save her child and burned to death with him.

sentences.zh: 太守劉悛以聞。

translations.literal: The Administrator Liu Jun reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Liu Jun reported it to the court.

sentences.zh: 又會稽人陳氏，有三女，無男。

translations.literal: Also, a man of Kuaiji surnamed Chen had three daughters and no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Also in Kuaiji, a man surnamed Chen had three daughters and no sons.

sentences.zh: 祖父母年八九十，老耄無所知，父篤癃病，母不安其室。

translations.literal: Their paternal grandparents were eighty or ninety, senile and knowing nothing; their father was gravely ill and paralyzed; their mother was discontent in the household.
translations.idiomatic: Their grandparents were nearly ninety, feeble and unaware; their father lay gravely ill and paralyzed; their mother was miserable at home.

sentences.zh: 值歲飢，三女相率於西湖採菱蓴，更日至市貨賣，未嘗虧怠。

translations.literal: In a year of famine the three daughters together went to West Lake to gather water chestnuts and lotus stems, taking turns day by day to sell them in the market, never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year the three daughters gathered water chestnuts and lotus stems at West Lake, taking turns selling them in the market without ever slackening.

sentences.zh: 鄉里稱為義門，多欲取為婦，長女自傷煢獨，誓不肯行。

translations.literal: The village called them a household of righteousness; many wished to take them as wives, but the eldest daughter, grieving her lonely state, swore she would not marry.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors called them a household of righteousness. Many men wished to marry them, but the eldest daughter, grieving their isolation, swore she would not leave.

sentences.zh: 祖父母尋相繼卒，三女自營殯葬，為菴舍墓側。

translations.literal: Before long their grandparents died one after another; the three daughters arranged the burials themselves and built a hut beside the graves.
translations.idiomatic: Their grandparents soon died in succession. The three daughters arranged the burials themselves and built a hut beside the tombs.

sentences.zh: 又永興概中里王氏女，年五歲，得毒病，兩目皆盲。

translations.literal: Also, a girl of the Wang family of Gaizhong village in Yongxing, at five years of age, contracted a poisonous illness and both her eyes went blind.
translations.idiomatic: Also in Yongxing, a Wang girl of Gaizhong village was five when a virulent illness left her blind in both eyes.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，年二十，父母死，臨屍一呌，眼皆血出，小妹娥舐其血，左目即開，時人稱為孝感。

translations.literal: By nature she was supremely filial; at twenty, when her parents died, at sight of their corpses she cried out once and blood flowed from both eyes; her younger sister E licked the blood, and her left eye at once opened—people of the time called this a response to filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: She was deeply filial by nature. At twenty, when her parents died, she cried out once over their bodies and blood streamed from both eyes. Her younger sister E licked the blood from her left eye, and it opened at once; people called it filial devotion moving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 縣令何曇秀不以聞。

translations.literal: The Magistrate He Tanxiu did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate He Tanxiu did not report it to the court.

sentences.zh: 又諸暨東洿里屠氏女，父失明，母痼疾，親戚相弃，鄉里不容。

translations.literal: Also, a girl of the Tu family of Dongwu village in Zhuji—her father was blind, her mother had a chronic illness; kinsmen abandoned them and the village would not shelter them.
translations.idiomatic: Also in Zhuji, a Tu girl of Dongwu village had a blind father and a mother with a chronic illness; relatives abandoned them and neighbors would not take them in.

sentences.zh: 女移父母遠住苧羅，晝樵采，夜紡績，以供養。

translations.literal: The daughter moved her parents far away to live at Zhuluo; by day she gathered firewood, by night she spun and wove, to support them.
translations.idiomatic: She moved her parents to Zhuluo. By day she gathered firewood; by night she spun and wove to support them.

sentences.zh: 父母俱卒，親營殯葬，負土成墳。

translations.literal: When both parents died, she personally arranged the funeral and burial, carrying earth on her back to raise the mound.
translations.idiomatic: When both parents died she arranged the funeral herself and carried earth on her back to build the mound.

sentences.zh: 忽聞空中有聲云：「汝至性可重，山神欲相驅使。

translations.literal: Suddenly she heard a voice in the air saying: "Your utmost sincerity is worthy of esteem; the mountain spirit wishes to employ you.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a voice in the air said: "Your devotion is extraordinary; the mountain spirit wishes to make use of you.

sentences.zh: 汝可為人治病，必得大富。」

translations.literal: You may heal people's illnesses and will surely gain great wealth."
translations.idiomatic: Heal the sick and you will surely grow very rich."

sentences.zh: 女謂是○魅，弗敢從，遂得病。

translations.literal: The girl took it for a demon and did not dare obey; she then fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: She took it for an evil spirit and refused; soon she fell ill.

sentences.zh: 積時，隣舍人有中溪蜮毒者，女試治之，自覺病便差，遂以巫道為人治疾，無不愈。

translations.literal: After some time a neighbor was stricken by stream-toad poison; the girl tried to treat him and felt her own illness improve at once, and thereafter practiced shamanic arts to heal people's illnesses—none went uncured.
translations.idiomatic: After a time a neighbor was poisoned by a stream toad. When she tried to treat him her own illness lifted, and from then on she healed people by shamanic means—always with success.

sentences.zh: 家產日益，鄉里多欲娶之，以無兄弟，誓守墳墓不肯嫁，為山賊劫殺。

translations.literal: The family's property grew day by day; many in the village wished to marry her, but because she had no brothers she swore to guard the graves and would not marry, and was killed by mountain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The family grew wealthier. Many men wished to marry her, but with no brothers she swore to guard the graves and refused; mountain bandits killed her.

sentences.zh: 縣令于琳之具言郡，太守王敬則不以聞。

translations.literal: The Magistrate Yu Linzhi reported the matter in full to the commandery, but the Administrator Wang Jingze did not pass it on.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Yu Linzhi reported the matter fully to the commandery, but Administrator Wang Jingze did not relay it to the court.

sentences.zh: 建武三年，吳興乘公濟妻姚氏生二男，而公濟及兄公願、乾伯竝卒，各有一子欣之、天保，姚養育之，賣田宅為娶婦，自與二男寄止隣家。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwu, Lady Yao, wife of Cheng Gongji of Wuxing, bore two sons; but Gongji and his elder brothers Gongyuan and Ganbo all died, each leaving one son—Xinzhi and Tianbao. Yao reared them, sold fields and houses to provide wives for them, and lodged herself and the two boys with a neighbor's family.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianwu, Lady Yao of Wuxing, wife of Cheng Gongji, bore two sons. Gongji and his brothers Gongyuan and Ganbo all died, each leaving a son—Xinzhi and Tianbao. Yao raised them, sold land and house to marry them off, and lodged herself and the boys with neighbors.

sentences.zh: 明帝詔為其二子婚，表門閭，復徭役。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming issued an edict arranging marriages for her two sons, erected a commemorative placard at her gate, and remitted her corvée obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming ordered marriages arranged for her two sons, set up a commemorative placard at her gate, and exempted her from corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 吳郡范法恂妻褚氏，亦勤苦執婦業。

translations.literal: Lady Chu, wife of Fan Faxun of Wu commandery, likewise labored diligently and upheld a wife's duties.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chu, wife of Fan Faxun of Wu commandery, was likewise diligent in every duty of a wife.

sentences.zh: 宋昇明中，孫曇瓘謀反亡命，褚謂其子僧簡曰：「孫越州先姑之姉子，與汝父親則從母兄弟，交則義重古人。

translations.literal: During the Shengming era of Song, Sun Tanwan rebelled and fled as an outlaw; Chu said to her son Sengjian: "Sun of Yuezhou is the elder sister's son of your late aunt; with your father he is a cousin on the mother's side, and in friendship their bond weighed as heavily as that of men of old.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengming era Sun Tanwan rebelled and fled. Chu told her son Sengjian: "Sun of Yuezhou is kin to your late aunt; he and your father are cousins, and their friendship was as weighty as that of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 逃竄脫不免，汝宜收之。」

translations.literal: Though he flees and hides, he cannot escape forever—you should take him in."
translations.idiomatic: Even fugitives cannot hide forever—you should shelter him."

sentences.zh: 曇瓘尋伏法，褚氏令僧簡往歛葬。

translations.literal: Before long Tanwan was executed by law; Lady Chu had Sengjian go to gather and bury him.
translations.idiomatic: Tanwan was soon executed. Lady Chu sent Sengjian to recover his body and bury him.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，永明中卒。

translations.literal: She was over seventy when she died during the Yongming era.
translations.idiomatic: She was over seventy when she died in the Yongming era.

sentences.zh: 僧簡在都，聞病馳歸，未至而褚已卒，將殯，舉尸不起，尋而僧簡至焉。

translations.literal: Sengjian was in the capital; hearing she was ill, he raced home, but before he arrived Chu had already died. When they were about to encoffin her, the corpse could not be lifted—then Sengjian arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Sengjian was in the capital. Hearing she was ill he rushed home, but she died before he arrived. When they tried to move her body for burial it would not lift—until Sengjian came.

sentences.zh: 封延伯字仲璉，渤海人也。

translations.literal: Feng Yanbo, courtesy name Zhonglian, was a native of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanbo, courtesy name Zhonglian, was from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 有學行，不與世人交，事寡嫂甚謹。

translations.literal: He had learning and conduct, did not associate with the world, and served his widowed sister-in-law with great care.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar of learning and integrity, he kept apart from worldly society and served his widowed sister-in-law with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿，舉秀才，不就。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as Registrar; he was recommended as a Cultivated Talent but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The province summoned him as Registrar and recommended him as Cultivated Talent, but he declined both.

sentences.zh: 後乃仕。

translations.literal: Only later did he take office.
translations.idiomatic: Only later did he enter office.

sentences.zh: 垣崇祖為豫州，啟太祖用為長史，帶梁郡太守。

translations.literal: When Yuan Chongzu was Governor of Yuzhou, he memorialized the Founding Emperor to appoint Yanbo Chief Clerk, concurrently serving as Administrator of Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Chongzu governed Yuzhou he recommended Yanbo to Emperor Gao as Chief Clerk, with concurrent appointment as Administrator of Liang commandery.

sentences.zh: 以疾自免，僑居東海，遂不至京師。

translations.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness and lived as a sojourner in Donghai, and thereafter never went to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned citing illness, settled in Donghai, and never went to the capital again.

sentences.zh: 三世同財，為北州所宗附。

translations.literal: Three generations held property in common and were looked to and attached to by the northern commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations held their wealth in common, and families throughout the north looked up to them.

sentences.zh: 豫章王辟中兵，不就，卒。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang summoned him as Central Army officer; he did not accept, and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang summoned him as a central army officer; he declined and died.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，大使巡行天下，義興陳玄子四世一百七十口同居。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan, when the imperial envoys toured the realm, Chen Xuanzi of Yixing had four generations and one hundred seventy persons living together under one roof.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan, as imperial envoys toured the empire, Chen Xuanzi of Yixing had four generations—one hundred seventy people—living together in one household.

sentences.zh: 武陵郡邵榮興、文獻叔八世同居。

translations.literal: In Wuling commandery, Shao Rongxing and Wen Xienshu had eight generations living together.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuling, Shao Rongxing and Wen Xienshu had eight generations living under one roof.

sentences.zh: 東海徐生之、武陵范安祖、李聖伯、范道根五世同居。

translations.literal: Xu Shengzhi of Donghai, and Fan Anzu, Li Shengbo, and Fan Daogen of Wuling had five generations living together.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shengzhi of Donghai and Fan Anzu, Li Shengbo, and Fan Daogen of Wuling each had five generations in one household.

sentences.zh: 零陵譚弘寶、衡陽何弘、華陽陽黑頭疏從四世同居，竝共衣食。

translations.literal: Tan Hongbao of Lingling, He Hong of Hengyang, and Yang Heitou of Huayang, distant cousins, had four generations living together, all sharing food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Hongbao of Lingling, He Hong of Hengyang, and Yang Heitou of Huayang—distant kinsmen—had four generations living together and sharing food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 詔表門閭，蠲租稅。

translations.literal: An edict ordered commemorative placards at their gates and remission of rents and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict honored their gates with commemorative placards and remitted their rents and taxes.

sentences.zh: 又蜀郡王續祖、華陽郝道福竝累世同爨。

translations.literal: Also Wang Suzu of Shu commandery and Hao Daofu of Huayang both had many generations sharing one hearth.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Suzu of Shu commandery and Hao Daofu of Huayang likewise had many generations cooking at one hearth.

sentences.zh: 建武三年，明帝詔表門閭，蠲調役。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwu, Emperor Ming issued an edict erecting commemorative placards at their gates and remitting their levies and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianwu Emperor Ming ordered commemorative placards at their gates and exempted them from levies and corvée.

sentences.zh: 吳達之，義興人也。

translations.literal: Wu Dazhi was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dazhi was from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 嫂亡無以葬，自賣為十夫客，以營冢槨。

translations.literal: When his sister-in-law died and there was no means to bury her, he sold himself as a ten-day laborer to provide coffin and grave.
translations.idiomatic: When his sister-in-law died and he could not afford a burial, he indentured himself for ten days' labor to pay for coffin and tomb.

sentences.zh: 從祖弟敬伯夫妻荒年被略賣江北，達之有田十畝，貨以贖之，與之同財共宅。

translations.literal: His father's younger cousin Jingbo and his wife, in a famine year, were seized and sold north of the Yangzi; Dazhi had ten mu of fields, which he sold to ransom them, and shared property and dwelling with them.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year his cousin Jingbo and his wife were captured and sold north of the Yangzi. Dazhi sold his ten mu of land to ransom them and shared home and property with them.

sentences.zh: 郡命為主簿，固以讓兄。

translations.literal: The commandery appointed him Registrar, but he firmly yielded the post to his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery appointed him Registrar, but he firmly yielded the post to his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 又讓世業舊田與族弟，弟亦不受，田遂閑廢。

translations.literal: He also yielded the family's hereditary fields to a younger clansman, but the younger man would not accept them either, and the fields lay idle.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave the family's ancestral fields to a younger kinsman, who refused them as well, and the land lay fallow.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，詔表門閭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan, an edict ordered a commemorative placard at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan an edict honored his gate with a commemorative placard.

sentences.zh: 河南辛普明僑居會稽，自少與兄共處一帳，兄亡，以帳施靈座，夏月多蚊，普明不以露寢見色。

translations.literal: Xin Puming of Henan, sojourning in Kuaiji, from youth had shared one canopy with his elder brother; when his brother died, he dedicated the canopy to the spirit seat. In summer when mosquitoes were many, Puming did not show displeasure at sleeping in the open.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Puming of Henan, living in Kuaiji, had shared one canopy with his brother from boyhood. When his brother died he gave the canopy to the spirit seat. In mosquito-ridden summers he slept in the open without complaint.

sentences.zh: 兄將葬，隣人嘉其義，賻助甚多，普明初受，後皆反之。

translations.literal: When his brother was about to be buried, neighbors admired his righteousness and gave many funeral gifts; Puming at first accepted them, but afterward returned them all.
translations.idiomatic: As his brother's burial approached, neighbors admired his devotion and gave generously. Puming accepted at first, then returned everything.

sentences.zh: 贈者甚怪，普明曰：「本以兄墓不周，故不逆來意。

translations.literal: The donors were greatly puzzled; Puming said: "At first I thought my brother's tomb was not complete, so I did not refuse your kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The donors were astonished. Puming said: "At first I thought my brother's tomb was incomplete, so I did not refuse your kindness.

sentences.zh: 今何忍亡者餘物以為家財。」

translations.literal: Now how could I bear to make the dead man's leftover goods into family wealth?"
translations.idiomatic: How could I now turn what belonged to the dead into family wealth?"

sentences.zh: 後遭母喪，幾至毀滅。

translations.literal: Later, when his mother died, he nearly destroyed himself in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his mother died, he nearly wasted away in mourning.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史豫章王辟為議曹從事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang, Governor of Yangzhou, summoned him as an aide in the Deliberation Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang, governor of Yangzhou, summoned him as an aide in the Deliberation Bureau.

sentences.zh: 年五十，卒。

translations.literal: At fifty he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty.

sentences.zh: 又有何伯璵，弟幼璵，俱厲節操。

translations.literal: There were also He Boyu and his younger brother Youyu, both strict in integrity and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: There were also He Boyu and his younger brother Youyu, both men of stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 養孤兄子，及長為婚，推家業盡與之。

translations.literal: He reared his elder brother's orphaned son, and when the boy grew up arranged his marriage and gave him the entire family estate.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his brother's orphaned son, married him when he came of age, and gave him the whole family estate.

sentences.zh: 安貧枯槁，誨人不倦，鄉里呼為人師。

translations.literal: Content in poverty and worn thin, he taught others without tiring; the village called him the people's teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He lived content in poverty and taught others tirelessly; neighbors called him their teacher.

sentences.zh: 郡守下車，莫不修謁。

translations.literal: Whenever a new commandery administrator took office, none failed to pay him a respectful visit.
translations.idiomatic: Every new commandery administrator paid him a respectful visit.

sentences.zh: 永明十一年，伯璵卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongming, Boyu died.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu died in the eleventh year of Yongming.

sentences.zh: 幼璵少好佛法，翦落長齋，持行精苦。

translations.literal: Youyu from youth loved the Buddhist Law, shaved his head and kept long fasts, and practiced with austere rigor.
translations.idiomatic: Youyu loved Buddhism from youth, took the tonsure, kept long fasts, and lived with austere devotion.

sentences.zh: 梁初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Liang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 兄弟年竝八十餘。

translations.literal: The brothers were both over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers lived past eighty.

sentences.zh: 王文殊，吳興故鄣人也。

translations.literal: Wang Wenshu was a native of Guzhang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenshu was from Guzhang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父沒虜，文殊思慕泣血，蔬食山谷三十餘年。

translations.literal: His father died among the barbarians; Wenshu mourned him with weeping blood, eating only vegetables in the hills and valleys for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: His father died in the north. Wenshu mourned until he wept blood, eating only plain food in the hills for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 太守謝板為功曹，不就。

translations.literal: The Administrator Xie Ban appointed him Merit Officer; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Xie Ban offered him the post of Merit Officer; he declined.

sentences.zh: 永明十一年，太守孔琇之表曰：「文殊性挺五常，心符三教。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongming, the Administrator Kong Xiuzhi memorialized: "Wenshu's nature upholds the five constant virtues; his heart accords with the three teachings.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yongming Administrator Kong Xiuzhi wrote: "Wenshu's nature embodies the five constant virtues; his heart accords with the three teachings.

sentences.zh: 以父沒獯庭，抱終身之痛，專席恒居，銜罔極之卹。

translations.literal: Because his father perished in the barbarian court, he bears lifelong grief, dwelling always on a solitary mat, cherishing boundless mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father died in the northern lands, he bears lifelong grief, living always on a solitary mat in boundless mourning.

sentences.zh: 服紵縞以經年，餌蔬菽以俟命，婚義滅於天情，官序空於素抱。

translations.literal: He wears hemp and plain silk year after year, eats vegetables and beans awaiting fate; marriage is extinguished in his natural feeling, and office ranks are void in his lifelong resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he wears hemp and plain cloth and eats only vegetables and beans; marriage has vanished from his heart, and office holds no place in his lifelong resolve.

sentences.zh: 儻降甄異之恩，牓其閭里。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would bestow the grace of special selection, let his village be honored with a placard."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would grant special favor, let his neighborhood be honored with a placard."

sentences.zh: 鬱林詔牓門，改所居為「孝行里」。

translations.literal: Emperor Yulin issued an edict honoring his gate and changed his dwelling place to "Lane of Filial Conduct."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yulin ordered his gate honored and renamed his neighborhood the Lane of Filial Conduct.

sentences.zh: 朱謙之字處光，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Qianzhi, courtesy name Chuguang, was a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qianzhi, courtesy name Chuguang, was from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父昭之，以學解稱於鄉里。

translations.literal: His father Zhaozhi was famed in the village for learning and understanding.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhaozhi was renowned in the district for learning.

sentences.zh: 謙之年數歲，所生母亡，昭之假葬田側，為族人朱幼方燎火所焚。

translations.literal: When Qianzhi was only a few years old, his birth mother died; Zhaozhi had her provisionally buried beside the fields, and the grave was burned by a brush fire set by his clansman Zhu Youfang.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianzhi was still a child his birth mother died. Zhaozhi had her buried provisionally by the fields, but kinsman Zhu Youfang's brush fire burned the grave.

sentences.zh: 同產姉密語之，謙之雖小，便哀戚如持喪。

translations.literal: His elder sister by the same mother told him in secret; though Qianzhi was small, he grieved as though in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: His elder sister told him in secret. Though he was still small, he grieved as though in full mourning.

sentences.zh: 年長不婚娶。

translations.literal: When he grew older he did not marry.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he never married.

sentences.zh: 永明中，手刃殺幼方，詣獄自繫。

translations.literal: During Yongming he killed Youfang with his own hand and went to prison to surrender himself.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming he slew Youfang with his own hand and surrendered himself to prison.

sentences.zh: 縣令申靈勗表上，別駕孔稚珪、兼記室劉璡、司徒左西掾張融牋與刺史豫章王曰：「禮開報仇之典，以申孝義之情；

translations.literal: The Magistrate Shen Lingxu reported upward; the Attendant Counselor Kong Zhigui, Acting Recorder Liu Lin, and Western Section Clerk of the Minister of Works Zhang Rong wrote a memorial to the Governor, the Prince of Yuzhang, saying: "Rites open the statute of vengeance to express filial and righteous feeling;
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Shen Lingxu reported the case. Kong Zhigui, Liu Lin, and Zhang Rong wrote to the Prince of Yuzhang, governor of the region: "Ritual law permits vengeance to express filial duty;

sentences.zh: 法斷相殺之條，以表權時之制。

translations.literal: law sets the statute against mutual killing to display the expedient regulation of the age.
translations.idiomatic: statutory law forbids killing to uphold the order of the age.

sentences.zh: 謙之揮刃斬冤，旣申私禮；

translations.literal: Qianzhi swung his blade and cut down his enemy, already fulfilling private obligation;
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi struck down his enemy and fulfilled his private duty;

sentences.zh: 繫頸就死，又明公法。

translations.literal: he bound his neck and submitted to death, thereby also clarifying public law.
translations.idiomatic: he bound himself and submitted to death, thereby honoring public law as well.

sentences.zh: 今仍殺之，則成當世罪人；

translations.literal: If he is now still put to death, he becomes a criminal of the age;
translations.idiomatic: If he is executed now, the court makes a criminal of him;

sentences.zh: 宥而活之，即為盛朝孝子。

translations.literal: if he is pardoned and allowed to live, he becomes a filial son of this flourishing dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: if he is pardoned, he becomes a filial son of this flourishing age.

sentences.zh: 殺一罪人，未足弘憲；

translations.literal: To kill one criminal is not enough to magnify the constitution;
translations.idiomatic: Executing one man does little to magnify the law;

sentences.zh: 活一孝子，實廣風德。

translations.literal: to spare one filial son truly broadens custom and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: sparing one filial son truly broadens moral influence.

sentences.zh: 張緒陸澄，是其鄉舊，應具來由。

translations.literal: Zhang Xu and Lu Cheng are old acquaintances of his village and should set forth the full circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xu and Lu Cheng, men of his district, should report the full circumstances.

sentences.zh: 融等與謙之竝不相識，區區短見，深有恨然。」

translations.literal: Rong and the others did not know Qianzhi at all; in our narrow view we deeply regret this.
translations.idiomatic: We do not know Qianzhi at all, yet in our limited view we feel deep regret at the case.

sentences.zh: 豫章王言之世祖，時吳郡太守王慈、太常張緒、尚書陸澄竝表論其事，世祖嘉其義，慮相復報，乃遣謙之隨曹虎西行。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang reported this to the Founding Emperor; at the time the Administrator of Wu commandery Wang Ci, the Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Xu, and the Minister of the Interior Lu Cheng all memorialized on the matter. The Founding Emperor admired his righteousness but feared mutual reprisals, and therefore sent Qianzhi west with Cao Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang reported to Emperor Gao. Administrator Wang Ci, Zhang Xu of the Ministry of Rites, and Lu Cheng of the Ministry of the Interior all memorialized on the case. The emperor admired Qianzhi's conduct but feared further blood feuds, and sent him west with Cao Hu.

sentences.zh: 將發，幼方子惲於津陽門伺殺謙之，謙之之兄選之又刺殺惲，有司以聞。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Youfang's son Yun lay in wait at Jinyang Gate and killed Qianzhi; Qianzhi's elder brother Xuanzhi in turn stabbed and killed Yun. The authorities reported this.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave, Youfang's son Yun ambushed and killed Qianzhi at Jinyang Gate. Qianzhi's brother Xuanzhi then stabbed Yun to death. Officials reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「此皆是義事，不可問。」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said: "These are all matters of righteousness and must not be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said: "These are all acts of righteousness and must not be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 悉赦之。

translations.literal: He pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 吳興沈顗聞而歎曰：「弟死於孝，兄殉於義。

translations.literal: Shen Yan of Wuxing, hearing of it, sighed and said: "The younger brother died for filial piety; the elder brother gave his life for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yan of Wuxing sighed and said: "The younger brother died for filial piety; the elder brother gave his life for righteousness.

sentences.zh: 孝友之節，萃此一門。」

translations.literal: The virtues of filial piety and brotherly devotion are gathered in this one household."
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety and brotherly devotion are gathered in this one family."

sentences.zh: 選之字處林，有志節，著辯相論。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi, courtesy name Chulin, had resolve and integrity and wrote Discourse on Distinguishing Physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhi, courtesy name Chulin, was a man of resolve and wrote a treatise on physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 幼時顧歡見而異之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: In his youth Gu Huan saw him and was struck by him, giving him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Gu Huan was impressed by him and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 官至江夏王參軍。

translations.literal: He reached office as Aide to the Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as aide to the Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 蕭叡明，南蘭陵人。

translations.literal: Xiao Ruiming was a native of Nan Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ruiming was from southern Lanling.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍諶從祖兄弟也。

translations.literal: He was a paternal cousin of the General-in-Chief Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was a cousin of General-in-Chief Zhen.

sentences.zh: 父孝孫，左軍。

translations.literal: His father Xiaosun was a commander of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiaosun commanded the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 叡明初仕員外殿中將軍。

translations.literal: Ruiming first served as Acting General of the Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Ruiming first served as acting general of the palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 少有至性，奉親謹篤。

translations.literal: From youth he had utmost sincerity and served his parents with careful devotion.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was deeply devoted and served his parents with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 母病躬禱，夕不假寐，及亡，不勝哀而卒。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill he prayed in person, and at night did not sleep; when she died, he could not bear his grief and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill he prayed in person and did not sleep at night. When she died his grief overwhelmed him and he died.

sentences.zh: 永明五年，世祖詔曰：「龍驤將軍、安西中兵參軍、松滋令蕭叡明，愛敬淳深，色養盡禮，喪過乎哀，遂致毀滅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming, the Founding Emperor issued an edict: "The Flying Dragon General, Central Army Aide of the Anxi Army, and Magistrate of Songzi, Xiao Ruiming, loved and revered with pure depth, nourished his parents with cheerful countenance and full ritual, and in mourning exceeded proper grief until he destroyed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongming Emperor Gao decreed: "Xiao Ruiming, Flying Dragon General, central army aide of the Anxi army, and magistrate of Songzi, loved his parents with pure devotion, served them with joyful ritual care, and mourned so deeply that he destroyed himself.

sentences.zh: 雖未達聖教，而一至可愍。

translations.literal: Though he did not attain the sage's teaching, his utmost sincerity is pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Though he did not attain the sage's teaching, his utmost devotion is deeply moving.

sentences.zh: 宜加榮命，以矜善人。

translations.literal: He should be granted posthumous honor to commend a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Let posthumous honors be granted to commend his goodness.

sentences.zh: 可贈中書郎。」

translations.literal: Let him be posthumously appointed Attendant of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously appointed Attendant of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 樂頤字文德，南陽涅陽人。

translations.literal: Le Yi, courtesy name Wende, was a native of Niyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Le Yi, courtesy name Wende, was from Niyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 世居南郡。

translations.literal: His family had long resided in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少而言行和謹，仕為京府參軍。

translations.literal: From youth his words and conduct were gentle and careful; he served as an aide in the capital commandery.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was gentle and careful in word and deed and served as an aide in the capital commandery.

sentences.zh: 父在郢州病亡，頤忽思父涕泣，因請假還，中路果得父凶問。

translations.literal: His father died of illness in Yingzhou; Yi suddenly thought of his father and wept, took leave to return, and on the road indeed received word of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: His father died of illness in Yingzhou. Yi suddenly wept for his father, asked leave to return home, and on the road received confirmation of his death.

sentences.zh: 頤便徒跣號咷，出陶家後渚，遇商人附載西上，水漿不入口數日。

translations.literal: Yi at once went barefoot, wailing loudly, left by Taojia Rear Ford, met a merchant who took him aboard going west, and for several days did not let water or broth pass his lips.
translations.idiomatic: Yi went barefoot, wailing loudly, left by Taojia Rear Ford, boarded a merchant boat heading west, and for days took neither water nor food.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇病，與母隔壁，忍痛不言，齧被至碎，恐母之哀己也。

translations.literal: Once when he fell ill and lay in the next room from his mother, he bore the pain in silence and bit his quilt to shreds, fearing his mother would grieve for him.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he was ill in the room next to his mother, he bore the pain in silence and bit his quilt to shreds lest she grieve for him.

sentences.zh: 湘州刺史王僧虔引為主簿，以同僚非人，弃官去。

translations.literal: Wang Sengqian, Governor of Xiangzhou, appointed him Chief Clerk, but because a colleague was unworthy he abandoned office and left.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengqian, governor of Xiangzhou, made him chief clerk, but when a colleague proved unworthy he resigned and left.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎庾杲之嘗往候，頤為設食，枯魚菜菹而已。

translations.literal: Yu Gao, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, once came to visit; Yi set out food for him—only dried fish and pickled vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gao of the Ministry of Personnel once visited. Yi served only dried fish and pickled vegetables.

sentences.zh: 杲之曰：「我不能食此。」

translations.literal: Gao said: "I cannot eat this."
translations.idiomatic: Gao said: "I cannot eat this."

sentences.zh: 母聞之，自出常膳魚羹數種。

translations.literal: His mother heard this and came out herself with several kinds of fish broth from their usual fare.
translations.idiomatic: His mother heard and brought out several kinds of fish soup from their usual fare.

sentences.zh: 杲之曰：「卿過於茅季偉，我非郭林宗。」

translations.literal: Gao said: "You go beyond Mao Jiwei; I am no Guo Linzong."
translations.idiomatic: Gao said: "You are more scrupulous than Mao Jiwei, but I am no Guo Linzong."

sentences.zh: 仕至郢州治中，卒。

translations.literal: He reached office as Administrative Advisor of Yingzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to administrative advisor of Yingzhou and died.

sentences.zh: 弟預亦孝，父臨亡，執其手以託郢州行事王奐，預悲感悶絕，吐血數升，遂發病。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yu was also filial; as their father lay dying he took Yu's hand and entrusted him to Wang Huan, Acting Governor of Yingzhou. Yu was overcome with grief, fainted, vomited several sheng of blood, and thereafter fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yu was also filial. As their father lay dying he took Yu's hand and entrusted him to Wang Huan, acting governor of Yingzhou. Yu fainted from grief, vomited blood, and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 官至驃騎錄事。

translations.literal: He reached office as Recorder under the Rapid Tiger General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to recorder under the Rapid Tiger General.

sentences.zh: 隆昌末，預謂丹陽尹徐孝嗣曰：「外傳藉藉，似有伊周之事，君蒙武帝殊常之恩，荷託付之重，恐不得同人此舉。

translations.literal: At the end of Longchang, Yu said to Xu Xiaosi, Governor of Danyang: "Rumors are widespread, as though there were a matter like Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; you have received Emperor Wu's extraordinary grace and bear the weight of his entrustment—I fear you cannot join in this undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Longchang Yu told Xu Xiaosi, governor of Danyang: "Rumors are rife, as though men plot like Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. You received extraordinary favor from Emperor Wu and bear a heavy trust—I fear you cannot join them.

sentences.zh: 人笑褚公，至今齒冷。」

translations.literal: People still laugh at Lord Chu, and teeth are cold to this day."
translations.idiomatic: People still mock Lord Chu, and the shame has not faded."

sentences.zh: 孝嗣心甚納之。

translations.literal: Xiaosi took this deeply to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosi took the warning deeply to heart.

sentences.zh: 建武中，為永世令，民懷其德。

translations.literal: During Jianwu he served as Magistrate of Yongshi, and the people cherished his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianwu he served as magistrate of Yongshi, and the people cherished his virtue.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 有一老嫗行擔斛蔌葉將詣市，聞預死，弃擔號泣。

translations.literal: An old woman was walking with a carrying-pole of vegetable leaves bound for market; hearing that Yu had died, she cast down her pole and wailed.
translations.idiomatic: An old woman carrying vegetable leaves to market heard of Yu's death, dropped her pole, and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 鴈門解仲恭，亦僑居南郡。

translations.literal: Xie Zhonggong of Yanmen also sojourned in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhonggong of Yanmen also lived in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 家行敦睦，得纖豪財利，輙與兄弟平分。

translations.literal: His household conduct was warm and harmonious; whatever trifling gain came his way, he at once divided equally with his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: His household was harmonious; whatever small gain came his way he divided equally with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 母病經時不差，入山採藥，遇一老父語之曰：「得丁公藤，病立愈。

translations.literal: His mother was ill for a long time without recovery; he went into the mountains to gather medicine and met an old man who told him: "Obtain Lord Ding's vine and the illness will be cured at once.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was ill for a long time. In the mountains gathering medicine he met an old man who said: "Find Lord Ding's vine and she will recover at once.

sentences.zh: 此藤近在前山際高樹垂下便是也。」

translations.literal: That vine is near at hand on the mountain ahead, hanging down from a tall tree—that is the one."
translations.idiomatic: It hangs from a tall tree on the ridge just ahead—that is the one."

sentences.zh: 忽然不見。

translations.literal: Suddenly he was gone.
translations.idiomatic: Then he vanished.

sentences.zh: 仲恭如其言得之，治病，母即差。

translations.literal: Zhonggong found it as the man had said, used it as medicine, and his mother recovered at once.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonggong found the vine as directed, treated his mother, and she recovered at once.

sentences.zh: 至今江陵人猶有識此藤者。

translations.literal: To this day people of Jiangling still recognize this vine.
translations.idiomatic: People in Jiangling still recognize this vine today.

sentences.zh: 江泌字士清，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Bi, courtesy name Shiqing, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bi, courtesy name Shiqing, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 父亮之，員外郎。

translations.literal: His father Liangzhi was an Attendant Cadet.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liangzhi was an attendant cadet.

sentences.zh: 泌少貧，晝日斫屟，夜讀書，隨月光握卷升屋。

translations.literal: Bi was poor in youth; by day he carved clogs, by night he read books, and following the moonlight he would take his scroll and climb onto the roof.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was poor as a youth. By day he carved clogs; by night he read, and when moonlight failed he would take his scroll and climb onto the roof to read.

sentences.zh: 性行仁義，衣弊，恐虱饑死，乃復取置衣中。

translations.literal: By nature his conduct was benevolent and righteous; when his clothes were worn, fearing the lice might starve to death, he would take them back and place them in his garments again.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was benevolent and righteous. When his clothes were worn he feared the lice might starve, so he would gather them back into his garments.

sentences.zh: 數日閒，終身無復虱。

translations.literal: Within a few days he never had lice again for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was never troubled by lice again.

sentences.zh: 母亡後，以生闕供養，遇鮭不忍食。

translations.literal: After his mother died, because he lacked the means to support her in life, when he encountered salmon he could not bear to eat it.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, remembering he had lacked the means to support her properly, he could not bear to eat salmon when he met it.

sentences.zh: 食菜不食心，以其有生意也。

translations.literal: He ate vegetables but not their hearts, because they still held the spark of life.
translations.idiomatic: He ate vegetables but not their hearts, for they still held life.

sentences.zh: 歷仕南中郎行參軍，所給募吏去役，得時病，莫有舍之者，吏扶杖投泌，泌親自隱卹，吏死，泌為買棺。

translations.literal: He served in turn as Aide on the March of the Southern General of the Gentlemen; a conscript clerk assigned to him left service and fell ill with a seasonal disease, and no one would shelter him. The clerk leaned on his staff and came to Bi; Bi personally cared for him in secret, and when the clerk died, Bi bought a coffin for him.
translations.idiomatic: He served as aide on the march of the Southern General. A conscript clerk under him fell ill after leaving service, and no one would take him in. The clerk came leaning on his staff; Bi cared for him himself, and when the clerk died Bi bought his coffin.

sentences.zh: 無僮役，兄弟共輿埋之。

translations.literal: Having no servants, he and his brothers together carried the coffin on a bier to bury him.
translations.idiomatic: With no servants, he and his brothers carried the coffin themselves to the burial.

sentences.zh: 領國子助教。

translations.literal: He held the post of Assistant Instructor at the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant instructor at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 乘牽車至染烏頭，見老翁步行，下車載之，躬自步去。

translations.literal: Riding in a small cart to Ranyawutou, he saw an old man walking, got down and gave him the cart, and went on foot himself.
translations.idiomatic: Riding a small cart to Ranyawutou, he saw an old man walking, gave him the cart, and walked on himself.

sentences.zh: 世祖以為南康王子琳侍讀。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor appointed him Reader to the Prince of Nankang, Zilin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao appointed him reader to Prince Zilin of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 建武中，明帝害諸王後，泌憂念子琳，詣誌公道人問其禍福。

translations.literal: During Jianwu, after Emperor Ming had killed the princes, Bi worried for Zilin and went to the Daoist master Zhigong to ask his fortune.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianwu, after Emperor Ming killed the princes, Bi worried for Zilin and asked the Daoist master Zhigong what fate held for him.

sentences.zh: 誌公覆香鑪灰示之，曰：「都盡。

translations.literal: Zhigong overturned the incense burner and showed him the ashes, saying: "All is gone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigong tipped over the incense burner and showed him the ashes. "All is gone," he said.

sentences.zh: 無所餘。」

translations.literal: Nothing remains."
translations.idiomatic: Nothing remains."

sentences.zh: 及子琳被害，泌往哭之，淚盡，繼之以血。

translations.literal: When Zilin was killed, Bi went to mourn him; his tears ran dry and were followed by blood.
translations.idiomatic: When Zilin was killed, Bi went to mourn him until his tears gave out and blood followed.

sentences.zh: 親視殯葬，乃去。

translations.literal: He personally oversaw the encoffining and burial, and only then departed.
translations.idiomatic: He personally oversaw the burial, then left.

sentences.zh: 時廣漢王侍讀嚴桓之亦哭王盡哀。

translations.literal: At the time Yan Huanzhi, Reader to the Prince of Guanghan, also mourned the prince with full grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Huanzhi, reader to the Prince of Guanghan, also mourned the prince with full grief.

sentences.zh: 泌尋卒。

translations.literal: Bi soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Bi soon died.

sentences.zh: 泌族人兖州治中泌，黃門郎悆子也，與泌同名。

translations.literal: A clansman of Bi named Bi, Administrative Advisor of Yanzhou, was the son of the Yellow Gate Attendant Yu and bore the same given name.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman also named Bi, administrative advisor of Yanzhou and son of Yellow Gate Attendant Yu, shared the same given name.

sentences.zh: 世謂泌為「孝江泌」以別之。

translations.literal: The age called this Bi "Filial Jiang Bi" to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: People called him "Filial Jiang Bi" to distinguish the two.

sentences.zh: 杜栖字孟山，吳郡錢唐人，徵士京產子也。

translations.literal: Du Qi, courtesy name Mengshan, was a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery, son of the Recluse Jingchan.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qi, courtesy name Mengshan, was from Qiantang in Wu commandery, son of the recluse Jingchan.

sentences.zh: 同郡張融與京產相友，每相造言論，栖常在側。

translations.literal: Zhang Rong of the same commandery was friends with Jingchan; whenever they visited each other to discuss learning, Qi was always at their side.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rong of the same commandery was a friend of Jingchan. Whenever they met to discuss learning, Qi was always present.

sentences.zh: 融指栖曰：「昔陳太丘之召元方，方之為劣。

translations.literal: Rong pointed to Qi and said: "When Chen Taqiu summoned Yuanfang, Yuanfang was the lesser.
translations.idiomatic: Rong pointed to Qi and said: "When Chen Taqiu summoned Yuanfang, Yuanfang was the lesser son.

sentences.zh: 以今方古，古人何貴。」

translations.literal: Comparing the present with antiquity, why should the ancients be esteemed?"
translations.idiomatic: Compared with today, why should the ancients be prized?"

sentences.zh: 栖出京師，從儒士劉瓛受學。

translations.literal: Qi left the capital and studied under the scholar Liu Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi left the capital to study under the scholar Liu Huan.

sentences.zh: 善清言，能彈琴飲酒，名儒貴遊多敬待之。

translations.literal: He was skilled in pure conversation, could play the zither and drink wine, and eminent scholars and noble travelers treated him with respect.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at pure conversation, played the zither, and drank wine; eminent scholars and noble travelers treated him with respect.

sentences.zh: 中書郎周顒與京產書曰：「賢子學業清標，後來之秀。

translations.literal: Zhou Yong, Attendant of the Secretariat, wrote to Jingchan: "Your worthy son's learning is clear and distinguished—a talent of the rising generation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yong of the Secretariat wrote to Jingchan: "Your worthy son's learning is clear and distinguished—a rising talent.

sentences.zh: 嗟愛之懷，豈知云已。

translations.literal: My sighing affection—how can I say it is ended?
translations.idiomatic: My affection for him—how can I say it has an end?

sentences.zh: 所謂人之英彥，若己有之也。」

translations.literal: What is called a brilliant man among people—I feel as though I already possess him."
translations.idiomatic: He is the sort of brilliant man one feels one already possesses."

sentences.zh: 刺史豫章王聞其名，辟議曹從事，仍轉西曹佐。

translations.literal: The Governor, the Prince of Yuzhang, hearing his fame, summoned him as an aide in the Deliberation Bureau, and he was later transferred to Western Section Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang, governor of the region, summoned him as an aide in the Deliberation Bureau and later made him western section assistant.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良數致禮接。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingling, Ziliang, repeatedly sent him courteous invitations.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling repeatedly honored him with invitations.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒何胤治禮，又重栖，以為學士，掌婚冠儀。

translations.literal: He Yin, Chancellor of the Imperial University, versed in ritual, also valued Qi and made him a University Scholar in charge of marriage and capping ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He Yin, chancellor of the Imperial University and expert in ritual, also valued Qi, made him a university scholar, and put him in charge of marriage and capping ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 以父老歸養，怡情壟畝。

translations.literal: Because his father was old, he returned home to support him and found contentment in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: When his father grew old he returned home to support him and found peace in the fields.

sentences.zh: 栖肥白長壯，及京產疾，旬日閒便皮骨自支。

translations.literal: Qi was plump, fair, tall, and strong; when Jingchan fell ill, within ten days he was reduced to skin and bone himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had been plump, fair, and strong; when Jingchan fell ill, within ten days Qi was skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 京產亡，水漿不入口七日，晨夕不罷哭，不食鹽菜。

translations.literal: When Jingchan died, Qi took no water or broth for seven days, wept morning and evening without cease, and ate neither salt nor seasoned vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingchan died, Qi took no food or drink for seven days, wept without cease morning and evening, and ate neither salt nor seasoned vegetables.

sentences.zh: 每營買祭奠，身自看視，號泣不自持。

translations.literal: Whenever he arranged and purchased offerings, he personally inspected them, wailing and unable to control himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he arranged offerings he inspected them himself, wailing beyond control.

sentences.zh: 朔望節歲，絕而復續，吐血數升。

translations.literal: On the first and fifteenth of the month and at festival seasons he would faint and revive, vomiting several sheng of blood.
translations.idiomatic: On new and full moons and festival days he would faint and revive, vomiting blood by the pint.

sentences.zh: 時何胤、謝朏竝隱東山，遺書敦譬，誡以毀滅。

translations.literal: At the time He Yin and Xie Tiao were both in seclusion on Eastern Mountain; they sent letters earnestly admonishing him against destroying himself.
translations.idiomatic: He Yin and Xie Tiao were then in seclusion on Eastern Mountain; they wrote urging him not to destroy himself in grief.

sentences.zh: 至祥禫，暮夢見其父，慟哭而絕。

translations.literal: When the auspicious and sacrificial mourning was reached, one evening he dreamed of his father, wailed in anguish, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the mourning rites he dreamed of his father one evening, cried out in grief, and died.

sentences.zh: 初，胤兄點見栖歎曰：「卿風韻如此，雖獲嘉譽，不永年矣。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Yin's elder brother Dian, seeing Qi, sighed and said: "With such grace as yours, though you win fine praise, you will not live long."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yin's brother Dian saw Qi and sighed: "With grace like yours, though you win praise, you will not live long."

sentences.zh: 卒時年三十六。

translations.literal: He died at the age of thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 當世咸嗟惜焉。

translations.literal: All the age sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: All who knew him mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，剡縣有小兒，年八歲，與母俱得赤班病。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, in Shan county there was a small boy eight years old who, with his mother, both contracted red-spot disease.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu an eight-year-old boy in Shan county and his mother both contracted red-spot fever.

sentences.zh: 母死，家人以小兒猶惡，不令其知。

translations.literal: When his mother died, the family, because the boy was still gravely ill, did not let him know.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died the family, fearing for the still-sick boy, kept it from him.

sentences.zh: 小兒疑之，問云：「母嘗數問我病，昨來覺聲羸，今不復聞，何謂也？」

translations.literal: The boy grew suspicious and asked: "Mother often asked after my illness; yesterday I felt her voice was weak, and today I hear her no more—what does this mean?"
translations.idiomatic: The boy grew suspicious and asked: "Mother often asked after my illness. Yesterday her voice sounded weak, and today I hear nothing—what has happened?"

sentences.zh: 因自投下牀，匍匐至母尸側，頓絕而死。

translations.literal: He then threw himself from the bed, crawled to his mother's corpse, and died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself from the bed, crawled to his mother's body, and died at once.

sentences.zh: 鄉隣告之縣令宗善才，求表廬，事竟不行。

translations.literal: Neighbors reported it to the Magistrate Zong Shancai, who requested a commemorative lodge; in the end the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors reported it to Magistrate Zong Shancai, who sought a commemorative lodge, but the request was never granted.

sentences.zh: 陸絳字魏卿，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Lu Jiang, courtesy name Weiqing, was a native of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jiang, courtesy name Weiqing, was from Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父閑，字遐業，有風概，與人交，不苟合。

translations.literal: His father Xian, courtesy name Xiaye, had moral bearing; in dealings with others he did not join company casually.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian, courtesy name Xiaye, was a man of moral bearing who did not make friends lightly.

sentences.zh: 少為同郡張緒所知，仕至揚州別駕。

translations.literal: In youth he was recognized by Zhang Xu of the same commandery and reached office as Attendant Counselor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zhang Xu of the same commandery recognized his talent; he rose to attendant counselor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，閑謂所親曰：「宮車晏駕，百司將聽於冢宰。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Xian said to those close to him: "The imperial carriage has departed at dusk; the hundred offices will heed the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Xian told those close to him: "The emperor is dead; the hundred offices will heed the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 主王地重才弱，必不能振，難將至矣。」

translations.literal: Our lord the prince has weighty territory but weak talent; he surely cannot restore order—trouble is coming."
translations.idiomatic: The prince holds great territory but lacks strength; he cannot restore order—trouble is coming."

sentences.zh: 乃感心疾，不復預州事。

translations.literal: He then developed a heart ailment and no longer took part in provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then fell ill at heart and withdrew from provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 刺史始安王遙光反，事敗，閑以綱佐被召至杜姥宅，尚書令徐孝嗣啟閑不預逆謀，未及報，徐世檦令殺之。

translations.literal: The Governor, the Prince of Shi'an, Yaoguang, rebelled; when the affair failed, Xian as a staff member was summoned to Old Woman Du's residence. The Minister of the Interior Xu Xiaosi memorialized that Xian had not joined the rebellion, but before a reply came, Xu Shizhen ordered him killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an rebelled and failed, Xian was summoned as a staff member to Old Woman Du's residence. Xu Xiaosi reported that Xian had not joined the plot, but before a reply came Xu Shizhen ordered him killed.

sentences.zh: 絳時隨閑，抱閑頸乞代死，遂并見殺。

translations.literal: Jiang was then with Xian; he embraced Xian's neck and begged to die in his place, and both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was with him, embraced his neck, and begged to die in his place; both were killed.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：澆風一起，人倫毀薄，抑引之教徒聞，珪璋之璞罕就。

translations.literal: The historian says: When shallow custom arises, human relations are ruined and thinned; the teaching of restraint and guidance is heard only in name, and uncut jade of ritual and virtue is rarely perfected.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When shallow custom spreads, human bonds grow thin; teachings of restraint are heard only in name, and uncut jade of virtue is rarely perfected.

sentences.zh: 若令事長移忠，儻非行舉，薑桂辛酸，容遷本質。

translations.literal: If one were to make serving elders shift into loyalty to the state, perhaps not by conduct and recommendation alone, ginger and cassia might grow bitter and sour, yet one's original nature might still be transformed.
translations.idiomatic: If serving elders were made to flow into loyalty to the state—not by recommendation alone—even through bitter trial one's original nature might yet be transformed.

sentences.zh: 而旌閭變里，問餼存牢，不過鰥寡齊矜，力田等勸。

translations.literal: Yet honoring gates and renaming lanes, sending inquiries and maintaining granaries, amounted to no more than equal pity for widowers and widows and encouragement of those who tilled diligently.
translations.idiomatic: Yet honoring gates, renaming lanes, sending grain, and maintaining granaries amounted to little more than pity for widows and orphans and rewards for diligent farmers.

sentences.zh: 其於扶獎名教，未為多也。

translations.literal: In supporting and commending the teaching of names and propriety, this was not much.
translations.idiomatic: In upholding moral teaching, it did not amount to much.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：孝為行首，義實因心。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Filial piety is the head of conduct; righteousness truly springs from the heart.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Filial piety leads all conduct; righteousness springs from the heart.

sentences.zh: 白華秉節，寒木齊心。

translations.literal: White flowers hold their nodes; cold trees share one heart.
translations.idiomatic: White flowers hold their stems; cold trees share one heart.

translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker in the source.
